```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)
```

```{r load-package}
library(mixeff)
```

A mixed-model report should describe the observations and grouping
units, model specification, estimates, and inference methods. It should
also record convergence problems and quantities that could not be
computed.

`mixeff` stores this information in the fitted object.
`reporting_table()` extracts individual sections, and `model_report()`
assembles them with software-version information. This article shows how
to use those tables and turn the results into methods and results prose.

## Example model

The example uses repeated weekly observations from clinics, with clinic
as the grouping factor.

```{r clinic-data, include = FALSE}
set.seed(42)
n_clinic <- 12L
n_per_clinic <- 6L
clinic <- factor(rep(seq_len(n_clinic), each = n_per_clinic))
week <- rep(0:(n_per_clinic - 1L), n_clinic)
treatment <- factor(
  rep(rep(c("usual", "coached"), each = n_per_clinic), length.out = length(week)),
  levels = c("usual", "coached")
)
clinic_shift <- rnorm(n_clinic, sd = 0.45)
score <- 7.2 - 0.28 * week - 0.55 * (treatment == "coached") +
  clinic_shift[as.integer(clinic)] + rnorm(length(week), sd = 0.35)
clinic_visits <- data.frame(score, week, treatment, clinic)
```

```{r show-data}
head(clinic_visits)
```

The analysis estimates average changes by week and treatment while allowing
clinics to have different baselines.

## Checking the specification

Before fitting, compile the model and read the design audit. This separates
formula interpretation from optimization and lets you check
the requested random-effects structure.

```{r compile-design}
spec <- compile_model(score ~ week + treatment + (1 | clinic), clinic_visits)
audit(spec)
```

```{r compile-checks, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(inherits(spec, "mm_spec"))
```

## Fitting and summarizing the model

Fit the model and inspect its summary:

```{r fit-model}
fit <- lmm(
  score ~ week + treatment + (1 | clinic),
  clinic_visits,
  control = mm_control(verbose = -1)
)
```

```{r fit-checks, include = FALSE}
stopifnot(inherits(fit, "mm_lmm"))
stopifnot(identical(fit_status(fit), "converged_interior"))
stopifnot(all(is.finite(fixef(fit))))
```

The overview table is a compact first pass over the fitted model: formula,
fitting mode, number of observations, fit status, inference availability, and
versioned artifact information.

```{r report-overview}
reporting_table(fit, "overview")
```

## Data and random-effects structure

The data-design section gives the grouping factors, their number of
levels, and rows per group.

```{r data-design}
reporting_table(fit, "data_design")
```

The random-term section records the grouping factor, basis, covariance
family, parameter count, and a description of each term.

```{r random-terms}
reporting_table(fit, "random_terms")
```

```{r design-report-checks, include = FALSE}
design <- reporting_table(fit, "data_design")$table
stopifnot(any(design$group == "clinic"))
stopifnot(all(design$group_levels[design$group == "clinic"] == n_clinic))
terms <- reporting_table(fit, "random_terms")$table
stopifnot(all(c("group", "basis", "covariance", "english") %in% names(terms)))
```

## Fixed effects and inference

`summary()` gives a familiar coefficient table. Use it for console review.

```{r model-summary}
coef_table <- summary(fit, method = "auto")$coef_table
knitr::kable(coef_table, digits = 4)
```

For report assembly, use `reporting_table()`. The fixed-effect section keeps
the estimate, uncertainty, statistic, p-value, method, row status, and
reliability label together.

```{r fixed-effect-report}
reporting_table(fit, "fixed_effects")
```

When you need to audit where those rows came from, request the audit view.

```{r fixed-effect-audit}
fixed_audit <- reporting_table(fit, "fixed_effects", view = "audit")$table
fixed_audit[, c("term", "method", "status", "reliability", "source")]
```

```{r fixed-effect-checks, include = FALSE}
fixed_report <- reporting_table(fit, "fixed_effects")$table
stopifnot(all(is.finite(fixed_report$estimate)))
stopifnot(any(is.finite(fixed_report$p_value)))
stopifnot(all(c("method", "status", "reliability") %in% names(fixed_report)))
stopifnot(all(fixed_audit$source == "fixed_effect_inference_table"))
```

## Turning the tables into methods and results prose

For this simulated example, the following prose uses the evaluated fit and
coefficient table. An applied report would also describe recruitment, exclusions,
and the study design; those facts cannot be inferred from a model object.

```{r report-prose-values, include = FALSE}
week_row <- summary(fit, method = "auto")$inference$table
week_row <- week_row[week_row$term == "week", , drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(nrow(week_row) == 1L, week_row$status == "available")
fmt <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 3)
```

> We fitted a Gaussian linear mixed model by restricted maximum likelihood to
> `r nobs(fit)` observations from `r nlevels(clinic_visits$clinic)` clinics.
> The model included fixed effects of week and treatment and a random intercept
> for clinic. Fixed-effect tests used the `r week_row$method` method. The
> optimizer reported an interior solution (`r fit_status(fit)`).
>
> Adjusting for treatment, the estimated weekly change in score was
> `r fmt(week_row$estimate)` points (SE `r fmt(week_row$std_error)`;
> p `r if (week_row$p_value < .001) "< .001" else paste("=", fmt(week_row$p_value))`).
> This estimate describes the common weekly slope assumed by the model.
> The simulated example does not establish a treatment effect in a clinical
> population.

## Fitted variance components

The random-effect table reports fitted variance components, together
with their source and availability status.

```{r random-effect-report}
reporting_table(fit, "random_effects")
```

```{r random-effect-checks, include = FALSE}
random_report <- reporting_table(fit, "random_effects")$table
stopifnot(any(random_report$kind == "variance"))
stopifnot(any(random_report$group == "Residual"))
stopifnot(any(is.finite(random_report$variance)))
```

## Unavailable results and other qualifications

Build the full model report when you want the section map, software
provenance, and list of unavailable or inapplicable fields.

```{r full-report}
report <- model_report(fit)
report
```

The `unavailable` section identifies missing or inapplicable fields and
other qualifications, with reason codes and a record of the action taken.

```{r unavailable-ledger}
reporting_table(report, "unavailable")
```

```{r unavailable-checks, include = FALSE}
unavailable <- reporting_table(report, "unavailable")$table
stopifnot(all(c("section", "field", "status", "reason") %in%
                names(unavailable)))
stopifnot(!any(unavailable$field ==
                 "stable_random_effect_variance_covariance_payload"))
```

## Assembling a report

Use the report sections as the source material for prose:

- `overview` records the formula, fit method, observations, fit status, and
  versioned artifact information.
- `data_design` records grouping-unit counts and rows per group.
- `random_terms` records the random-effects specification and its design
  support.
- `fixed_effects` records estimates and inference labels.
- `random_effects` records fitted variance components.
- `unavailable` records unavailable quantities and their reasons.

Use `vignette("inference", package = "mixeff")` for term tests, contrasts, and
model comparisons. Use the introduction vignette's save-and-revive section
(`vignette("mixeff", package = "mixeff")`) for reports based on saved fits.
